title: rename ci env keys to REDWOOD_CI_* and add backward-compat shim
author: Maya Singh
body:
Summary: Standardize CI / build environment variable names under the REDWOOD_CI_ prefix, add a compatibility shim that maps legacy keys at runtime, and update lint/test pipelines + release automation to consume the new keys. This is primarily a repo hygiene / stability change so downstream scripts and Private install artifacts have a single canonical set of environment names.

Motivation and context: Over time multiple repos and scripts used different env names (CI_TOKEN, RELEASE_CHANNEL, CI_REGION, etc.). That divergence caused subtle breakage during release automation and when switching runners. This PR standardizes names, reduces cognitive load (all CI keys start with REDWOOD_CI_), and avoids leaking non-prefixed keys to runtime. To reduce customer and infra impact we introduce a small compatibility shim: at pipeline start the shim reads legacy names and populates REDWOOD_CI_* equivalents if not present. We also updated all Redwood workflows, the private-installer helper, and local dev scripts to set the new keys directly.

This PR includes:
- Rename mapping and central file: infra/ci/env-schema/README.md and infra/ci/env-schema/keys.json (keys.json is a simple mapping of legacy->canonical; used by the shim and by the docs). 
- Compatibility shim: infra/ci/bin/compat-env.sh and compat-env.ps1. The script is intentionally minimal (no network calls) and documented for maintainers. It runs as a pre-step in workflows.
- GH Actions: workflows/ci.yml and workflows/release.yml updated to use REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN, REDWOOD_CI_REGION, REDWOOD_CI_CHANNEL.
- Lint & test updates: scripts/test_runner.sh and tooling/lint/bootstrap now export canonical env keys for test profiles and hermetic runners.
- Release automation: reltool/automation.py reads REDWOOD_CI_* keys; we added fallback path for legacy keys for one release window (see rollout plan).
- Migration docs: docs/dev/ci-env-migration.md with a small checklist for on-call and SRE.
- Fix: a flaky unit test in pkg/runtime/fixture_loader_test.go caused spurious failures when env names mixed; refactored fixture loader to accept explicit env map in tests and removed global reliance.

Checklist (manual steps):
- [x] Add canonical key list and docs (docs/dev/ci-env-migration.md)
- [x] Add compat shim for bash + powershell
- [x] Update GH workflows and action inputs to use REDWOOD_CI_*
- [x] Update reltool and example deploy scripts
- [x] Run full CI matrix, smoke on release branch, and staged rollout
- [x] Communicate on #infra and tag teams in Linear

Migration / Rollout plan:
1) Merge this PR to main with compat shim in place.
2) Leave legacy keys accepted for 2 release cycles; compat shim emits a CRITICAL warning in logs when it sees legacy keys (so callers can be updated).
3) After 2 cycles, open a small follow-up PR to tighten the shim (change warning -> failure) and then deprecate legacy keys from docs.

Testing performed:
- Ran full lint/unit/integration matrix on the branch: all checks green.
- Manual run of release.yml in a sandbox org using the compat shim verified no change to release artifacts.
- Local smoke: private-installer CI image built with both legacy and canonical env sets.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: third-party integrations or customer scripts that set legacy keys may break if the shim is bypassed. Mitigation: shim is a default pre-step in workflows; docs and infra Slack announcement were posted; Linear tasks created to follow up with top callers.
- Risk: accidental leakage of non-prefixed env vars. Mitigation: lint rule added in tooling/lint/preflight to flag non-REDWOOD_CI_ keys in workflow files; this is advisory for the first cycle.

Commits (summary):
- chore(ci): add env-schema/keys.json and README
- feat(ci): add compat-env.sh and compat-env.ps1
- refactor(ci): update workflows and reltool to prefer REDWOOD_CI_* keys
- fix(tests): refactor fixture loader to accept env map
- docs: add dev/ci-env-migration.md and release notes

Files / areas changed (high-level):
- infra/ci/env-schema/keys.json
- infra/ci/bin/compat-env.sh
- infra/ci/bin/compat-env.ps1
- .github/workflows/ci.yml
- .github/workflows/release.yml
- reltool/automation.py
- scripts/test_runner.sh
- tooling/lint/preflight (lint rule)
- pkg/runtime/fixture_loader_test.go (test refactor)
- docs/dev/ci-env-migration.md

Follow-ups (planned):
- Remove legacy key acceptance after two release cycles (ENG-6190)
- Add a CI telemetry metric to count legacy-key usage (ENG-6202)
- Update private-installer templates and Partner integration docs within 1 month

Related: Linear ENG-6123 (env standardization), ENG-6190 (shim hardening), SUP-4312 (customer-reported release flaky due to mixed env).
commits: chore(ci): add env schema and docs
feat(ci): compat shim for legacy env keys
refactor: switch workflows and reltool to canonical keys
changes: Updated GitHub workflows to export REDWOOD_CI_*
Updated reltool to prefer canonical keys with fallback
Added lint preflight rule to flag non-REDWOOD_CI env usage
review_comments: Evan Park: Please ensure compat-env.sh is POSIX-safe — noted two uses of bash-specific arrays. (reply) Maya: updated to avoid arrays and added a small compat test.
Jordan Lee: Can we add an env telemetry event? We should track legacy key usage. (reply) Maya: Added follow-up ENG-6202 to add telemetry; won't block merge.
Priya Malhotra: Reltool change looks good, but please add a unit test for the fallback path. (reply) Maya: Added unit test reltool/test/test_env_fallback.py and it passes in CI.
release_notes: Standardize CI env keys to REDWOOD_CI_ prefix; add backwards-compatibility shim and update workflows. No runtime behavior change expected. Follow-up to remove legacy keys after 2 release cycles.
notes_for_oncall: If a pipeline suddenly fails with missing REDWOOD_CI_* key, check whether compat-env.sh ran (pre-step) and search logs for 'legacy env detected' warnings. Re-run workflow with compat shim enabled if needed.
post_merge_tasks: Announce change in #infra and update on-call runbook
Open PR to tighten shim after two release cycles
